stories.notes: Cross-market (GO, UP, MX) live preview feature with no acceptance criteria and null spec. Complex feature requiring real-time content rendering, CMS integration, and likely iframe/SSR coordination. openspec must elaborate requirements, define AC, and assess whether story splits are needed per market. speckit must harden with security checks (iframe sandboxing, XSS), edge cases (draft vs published state, market-specific rendering), and testability criteria.

agentContributions.notes: Live Preview is a novel capability — no existing implementation found in the shown code. The attachment point is useContent, the single hook through which all 236+ components fetch content via getContentByKey. Contentstack Live Preview integration must plug in there. The IContentstackLink deprecation comment in ContentstackLink.tsx references cx-shared as the source of truth for that interface, suggesting the shared library may already have Live Preview utilities to reuse. Cannot confirm without seeing useContent source or cx-shared internals.

Openspec provided zero acceptance criteria, so I authored the full list. Criteria are derived from the story title ('Live Preview of Content in CMS'), the listed technical files (useContent.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx, ContentstackContext.tsx, contentCard.ts), and standard Live Preview integration concerns. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: I have not seen the contents of the four referenced files. AC-2 assumes useContent exposes content by key; AC-6 assumes ContentstackLink renders reference data; AC-12 assumes an IContent interface exists. These may need adjustment once file contents are reviewed. AC-7 (origin validation) may be handled by the Contentstack SDK itself — if so, this AC can be relaxed to verify the SDK is configured with the correct origin rather than reimplementing validation. AC-10 (selective re-render) may be inherently satisfied by React's reconciliation if useContent is keyed properly, but is stated as an observable outcome to guard against naive global-state updates.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents contributed non-overlapping value: openspec provided architectural reconnaissance (identifying useContent as the integration attachment point and flagging cx-shared as a potential source of Live Preview utilities), while speckit authored a full acceptance-criteria set from scratch with transparent caveats. However, openspec under-delivered — it provided context but no requirements elaboration, leaving speckit to carry the full AC authoring burden. Speckit's ACs are built on assumptions about four referenced files (useContent.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx, ContentstackContext.tsx, contentCard.ts) that neither agent actually read, so the criteria may need adjustment once file contents are reviewed. Human review is warranted to validate the assumptions and confirm the ACs align with actual code structure.
